Subject: Zephyr - concurrent streaming load plan & SLO validation

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the chat today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned before we get SRE involved:

- Goal: Validate that Redwood meets Zephyr's production SLOs for streaming inference (99th pct latency <= 350ms for streaming responses, sustained throughput 12k tokens/sec, concurrency 300 active streams).
- Scope: customer-driven load run using your representative streaming scenarios (small messages and long-payload streams). We will provide a k6 profile and can support a Locust alternative if you prefer.
- Test artifacts we'll share: k6 script, allowlist IPs, short-lived test service accounts, expected SLO matrix.

Proposed test window: Fri Nov 20, 10:00-14:00 PT (4 hours). Please confirm whether that works for your SRE and whether Zephyr needs us to shift earlier/later.

Action items for you: please send the list of external IPs (or confirm you want ours to be allowlisted), and the test accounts you want us to accept for auth. If the SRE team prefers Locust, flag that and we will translate the profile.

I've cc'd Aisha to keep sales manager visibility. Once you confirm window and allowlist approach I'll loop in Rishi and Dev (SEs) with the tech details.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Alex Stewart <alex.stewart@zephyr.ai>

Subject: Re: Zephyr - concurrent streaming load plan & SLO validation

Thanks Marissa — that summary matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) SLO tolerance: 99th pct streaming latency target is 350ms, but we allow a 10% excursion during warm-up — would like to see steady-state within target for at least 30 continuous minutes.
2) Throughput verification: we will validate both sustained token throughput and per-connection bandwidth. Expectation: reach 12k tokens/sec sustained with peaks up to 18k tokens/sec.
3) Concurrency: 300 active streams is our baseline. We will also run a short spike test to 500 for failure-mode observations.

Allowlisting: Zephyr prefers to provide IPs on our side (we will give you CIDR ranges). SRE will coordinate the exact ranges and timing.

Test accounts: we'll provision two short-lived API keys (one full-feature, one throttled) and send them to your SEs via the secure channel.

Window: Fri Nov 20 10:00-14:00 PT is good for SRE. If Redwood needs more ramp time, let us know.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering, Zephyr AI
alex.stewart@zephyr.ai

Team — forwarding Zephyr's confirmations. High level ask for SEs/SRE at Redwood:

- Provide k6 script tuned for streaming (we'll attach base profile). If you prefer Locust, call it out.
- Prepare a short runbook for the test window (ramp schedule, monitoring dashboards, rollback criteria).
- Generate allowlist IPs to share (we will also accept their CIDR ranges if easier).
- We'll be given two test API keys from Zephyr; ensure throttled key meets their described behavior.

Can Rishi own the k6 profile and monitoring dashboard? Dev, can you prepare the runbook and coordinate allowlist acceptance? Would appreciate a quick sync today (15-20 min) to confirm test steps.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Alex Stewart <alex.stewart@zephyr.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 13:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Zephyr - concurrent streaming load plan & SLO validation

Marissa / team — I'll own the k6 script and dashboard. Notes and technical assumptions below:

- k6 streaming approach: we'll use k6 websocket & http/2 helpers to emulate streaming token frames. Provided base profile includes three scenarios: short chat (avg 12 tokens/msg), medium stream (avg 150 tokens), long stream (avg 1.2k tokens) with proportional concurrency split (60/30/10).
- Ramp: 20m progressive ramp to 300 concurrent streams, then 3.5hr steady state at target throughput, followed by a 20m cool-down. Spike test to 500 concurrent streams for 10 min at the end.
- Metrics: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec aggregate, CPU/GPU utilization per instance, KV-cache hit rate, socket churn. We'll instrument the Redwood dashboard and share a live link during the window.
- Auth: we'll accept Zephyr's two short-lived API keys. Please confirm: keys will be bearer tokens with x-expire header; we'll add them to the test client.
- Fallbacks: If streaming stalls, test harness will degrade to batched HTTP mode; we'll capture differences and fall back to a diagnostic run.

I attached allowlist template and example IPs for Zephyr to fill (we will accept either their CIDRs or add our egress IPs if they prefer).

I'll push k6 profile v2 to the shared Drive by EOD today and post the run command and env var list.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

All — thanks for fast turnaround and clarity. Confirming final checklist before Friday's window:

- Zephyr SRE to post CIDR file by 09:30 PT (Priya: got it).
- Redwood SEs: Rishi will share k6 v2 link and live dashboard by 08:30 PT. Dev will publish short runbook with ramp steps and rollback criteria to the shared Drive.
- Zephyr to provision two test API keys via secure vault link; Redwood will retrieve and validate before 09:15 PT.
- Allowlist: Redwood will accept Zephyr CIDRs; we will also provide egress IPs if any outbound callbacks are required.
- Success criteria: 99th pct streaming latency <= 350ms steady-state for >=30min; sustained tokens/sec >=12k; concurrency handling up to 300 with observed graceful degradation at 500.

I'll set up a 30-min post-test readout slot for 14:30 PT to review results and next steps (Inc. any tuning and potential Dedicated capacity sizing if needed).

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the run.
